notes: With a Gemini key set, the lyrics are timed from the recording itself: the song’s own audio goes with the request, so each line is placed against the voice singing it instead of against a share of the song’s length. A sheet that already arrived with timestamps can be timed again, and the old ones are no longer sent to the model with the words.
The song whose lyrics are open is the song that gets timed, whichever list it came from: a song played straight from a search used to answer “No track info.” and could never use the key.

The words still outrank the model: a timing that rewrites, translates, drops or evenly spaces the lines is refused, a line put inside an instrumental break is pulled back to where the voice resumes, and every stamp is snapped onto a real rise in the recording.

A music video that runs shorter than half the song is never played as the video any more. A teaser, a short or a cut of the intro used to be attached whenever the search found nothing better — and because the film carried the sound, the song was paused underneath it, so everything stopped at the clip’s last second.

That is why the lyrics kept stopping at one minute: the sheet follows the film’s clock while the film is what is sounding. A clip now gets one search for the song’s full cut, a film that ends while the song has minutes left hands the sound back to the song, and the sheet will not take a clock shorter than the song — so the words run to the last verse.
The split Studio/Tools tab is readable on the tab you are on: both names are painted in the readable on-accent colour instead of the accent colour that fills the tile.
